#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/ reached the disk or the
# folder's .git, nor any spec-side file under another branch (the records
# branch keeps spec-side outputs). Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

fail=0
for p in vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
# Spec-side outputs can reach .git another way: each record on the records
# branch keeps the harness's and the spec experiments' outputs, and fetching
# a record's files wholesale brings their blobs in (it happened once, in
# M1; docs/EXPOSURE.md). So under every branch, remote branch included, a
# file under a folder named harness/ or spec-experiments/, or under
# vendor/emulator/ or sessions/spec/, at any depth, must be missing too.
# Trees are in a blob-less clone, so this reads no file.
have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname)' refs/heads refs/remotes \
    | sort -u | while read -r c; do GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r "$c"; done \
    | awk -F '\t' '{ split($1, m, " ") } m[2] == "blob" && $2 ~ /(^|\/)(harness|spec-experiments|vendor\/emulator|sessions\/spec)\// { print m[3] }' \
    | sort -u | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
[ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have spec-side output or source file(s) reached through a branch (the records branch?) are in .git"; fail=1; }
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/ reached the disk or the
# folder's .git, nor any spec-side file under another branch (the records
# branch keeps spec-side outputs). Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

fail=0
for p in vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
# Spec-side outputs can reach .git another way: each record on the records
# branch keeps the harness's and the spec experiments' outputs, and fetching
# a record's files wholesale brings their blobs in (it happened once, in
# M1; docs/EXPOSURE.md). So under every branch, remote branch included, a
# file under a folder named harness/ or spec-experiments/, or under
# vendor/emulator/ or sessions/spec/, at any depth, must be missing too.
# Trees are in a blob-less clone, so this reads no file.
have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname)' refs/heads refs/remotes \
    | sort -u | while read -r c; do GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r "$c"; done \
    | awk -F '\t' '{ split($1, m, " ") } m[2] == "blob" && $2 ~ /(^|\/)(harness|spec-experiments|vendor\/emulator|sessions\/spec)\// { print m[3] }' \
    | sort -u | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
[ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have spec-side output or source file(s) reached through a branch (the records branch?) are in .git"; fail=1; }
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"
----

content.content:
<!--
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
-->

# Plan

An original, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket
synthesizer (JieLi AC791N: two pi32v2 cores, 240x240 LCD, key matrix, rotary
encoders, I2S audio), written clean-room so it can ship inside the
F-Emulator iOS app, provably independent of the FM-1's GPL community
firmwares.

Each milestone has its own prompt (`docs/prompts/<Mx>.md`) and its own fresh
session. Roles are defined in CONTRIBUTING.md; requirement IDs are in
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md.

## Milestones

### M0a: foundation (firmware side)
Repo, rules, roles, exposure register, records, signing, toolchain, SDK, CI.
No firmware code yet; a placeholder translation unit proves the pipeline.
- Requirements: R-PROC-1..4, R-REC-1..2, R-REPRO-1..5, R-BUILD-1,
  R-LIC-1..2, R-PUB-1..2, R-CLEAN-1..5.
- Done when: the repo exists with the bootstrap commit and rulesets; CI on a
  pull request runs reuse lint, the commit-message check, the low-profile
  check, the toolchain container build with its checksum and the
  byte-for-byte double build; the owner's signed merge produces the first
  record with a pending OpenTimestamps proof; `tools/reproduce` works;
  EXPOSURE.md and PROVENANCE.md are complete; nothing forbidden was opened.
- Status 2026-10-22: pull request #1 merged as `2fd28219`. Its record
  (`records/2fd28219…/` on `records`) has 13 checks PASS and C-MERGE FAIL
  under the merge rule of the time (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge policy and its
  history"), with a pending OpenTimestamps proof (three calendars).
  `tools/reproduce 2fd28219` on the owner's Mac: REPRODUCED (both outputs
  match the record).

### M0b: harness (spec side)
Vendor the emulator crates `fm1-isa`, `fm1-core`, `fm1-soc` from the public
upstream `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` at a pinned commit, with its MIT licence,
into `vendor/emulator/` (never the rest of that repo). Build the harness: a
Rust library and `fwtest` CLI that boots a raw image, runs N emulated ms with
a timed input script, captures RAM, the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV)
and instructions per audio block, detects halts, compares golden files, and
emits JUnit and JSON.
- Requirements: R-REPRO-*, R-LIC-*, new harness requirements (R-HARN-*).
- Done when: `fwtest` runs in CI from a pinned container, its outputs are
  deterministic, and `tools/clean-setup.sh` excludes `vendor/emulator/` and
  `harness/` from clean clones.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0b, spec side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Setup** (pull request #3): the spec folder, its hand-made settings kept
    and guarded, M0a's transcripts archived in `sessions/clean/`; spec-side
    transcripts go to `sessions/spec/`, which clean folders leave out and
    deny (R-SEP-2).
  - **Emulator** (pull request #4): three crates vendored at upstream commit
    `43ed5580`, reproducible by `tools/fetch-emulator.sh` with a tree hash
    (C-EMU-PIN). One patch, to the workspace manifest only.
  - **Harness** (pull request #4): `fwtest`, a Rust library and CLI with no
    third-party crates, built offline in a container on digest-pinned bases
    (Rust 1.99.0). It boots raw images, takes timed inputs, captures RAM,
    the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV), instructions per audio block
    and the debug console, tells faults, halts and hangs apart, compares
    golden files, and writes JSON and JUnit. Its own tests: 23 cargo tests
    and a 13-case suite on 12 small test images built with the pinned
    toolchain. The suite's outputs were byte-identical in two amd64
    containers at different paths and on Apple Silicon natively.
  - **Separation**: docs/HARNESS.md (the clean side's manual) and
    docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md; checks C-SEP-TERMS, C-CLEAN-FOLDER and
    C-FWTEST-PIN; requirements R-SEP-1..3 and R-HARN-1..10.
  - **Merged**: #3 as `0ad38801`, #4 as `5d4d6fd2`. The records for both
    merges are PASS, with every check run, none skipped. The second
    record's `harness/` holds the suite's JSON, JUnit and output hashes.
  - **Publishing**: `.github/workflows/fwtest-image.yml` pushed the image
    built from `5d4d6fd2` as
    `ghcr.io/japes98/small-beeps@sha256:fa74baf9…` (public; pulls without
    logging in). `config/fwtest-image` pins it, and the suite run through
    `tools/fwtest` with it gives all 47 output files with the same SHA-256
    as that record.
  - **Before the next clean session**, in the clean folder, from a shell:
    `export GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; git fetch origin;` then
    `env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git merge -q --no-stat --ff-only origin/main`
    (only the folder's own files are fetched; without `--no-stat` the merge
    summary downloads the excluded files to count their lines, as
    happened in clean maintenance session 1), then `tools/clean-setup.sh`.
    Its live settings predate the new deny rule and the lazy-fetch
    setting, so its banner would otherwise say CONFIG MISMATCH. From then
    on, `tools/clean-update.sh` updates it.

### M0c: hardware spec (spec side)
`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols),
each with its source. Facts whose only source is the emulator are marked as
such. It also maps fwtest's key, LED and encoder numbers to the panel and
the key matrix, and covers what docs/HARNESS.md defers to it (the memories,
the second core's release, the audio output's format and rate, the debug
message register), and answers any open spec requests.
- Done when: reviewed for "facts, not code" before the firmware side reads it.
- Requirements: R-SPEC-1..4.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0c, spec side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Start** (pull request #7): the prompt; M0b's transcript archived in
    `sessions/spec/`, clean maintenance session 1's in `sessions/clean/`
    with its merge summary's spec-side file names redacted (the archiver
    now does this for clean transcripts); ten of that session's commands
    listed in `sessions/REVIEWED.json` with the owner's approval.
  - **Clean updates** (pull request #8): `tools/clean-update.sh` and the
    steps above merge with `--no-stat -q`; C-CLEAN-FOLDER updates a clean
    clone across a commit that changes `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/`
    and checks none of their blobs arrive (a control merge with a summary
    fetches 6).
  - **The spec** (pull request #9): `docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, 47 entries
    (HW-1 to HW-47: 38 confirmed, 9 emulator-only) for M0d to M4, flash
    preliminary for M7, and 12 open questions. Sources: the JieLi SDK,
    FM-1-RE's hardware documents, the ST7789V datasheet, the panel's
    printed labels (the owner's app screenshot, `docs/sources/`, and
    M-VAVE's product photo, cited by URL), and nine spec-side black-box
    experiments in fwtest (E-1 to E-9, `harness/spec-experiments/`, spec
    side), rerun in CI by C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS. Reviewed by a fresh
    subagent given only the spec, CONTRIBUTING.md and the rules;
    its report and the response are in `docs/reviews/M0c-spec-review.md`.
  - **Checks**: C-SPEC-LINT (entries, sources, standings, no code, IDs
    kept), C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS; C-SEP-TERMS now scans the two doors for
    emulator-only identifiers.
  - **Found on the way**: while an image waits, fwtest's captures can come
    several milliseconds late; docs/HARNESS.md ("Time") now says so.
  - No spec requests were open. M0d (firmware side) is next.

### M0d: smallest firmware (firmware side)
Startup, linker script and `main` (a marker word, a heartbeat), written only
from `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the SDK and FM-1-RE's documents; booted and checked
with `fwtest`. Design choices explained in docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md.
- Requirements: R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5, R-BUILD-1, R-BUILD-2.
- Done when: CI boots the image in the harness and the record shows the
  marker word and heartbeat.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0d, firmware side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Start**: the clean folder fast-forwarded with lazy fetching off;
    `tools/clean-update.sh` passed. Nothing was left to archive (the
    session the prompt named is this one); `tools/check-transcripts.py`
    PASS.
  - **The firmware** (`firmware/`): `crt0.S` sets the stack and calls
    `sb_start`, which copies initialised data, clears zeroed data and runs
    `main`. `main` writes the marker `SB0D` to a four-word beacon at
    `0x01C00000` and a line to the debug console, then keeps a heartbeat
    of one beat per millisecond of TIMER4, without interrupts. Freestanding
    C11 with `-nostdinc`, no library code of any kind, one assembly file.
    Sources: HW-1 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26 (all confirmed; no
    emulator-only fact relied on), the SDK's `WL82.h`, and our own
    toolchain experiments (PROVENANCE P-13 to P-15).
  - **Size**: code 252, data 4, bss 20 bytes; raw image 256 bytes; stack
    4 KiB reserved. Recorded by C-FW-SIZE (R-BUILD-2).
  - **Tests**: `tests/fw/boot.suite` through `tools/fwtest`, checked by
    `tools/fw-suite.py` (C-FW-SUITE): golden marker, console line and top
    of RAM; a one-second heartbeat whose time base agrees with fwtest's
    emulated time within 10 µs. Requirements R-BOOT-3 to R-BOOT-5 and
    R-BUILD-2 added.
  - **Found on the way**: fwtest counts the heartbeat's polling loop as
    waiting even though it stores to RAM each pass, so captures came up to
    1.6 ms late; the beacon's stored tick count keeps the timing checks
    exact (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md). `ld --oformat binary` resolved a data
    address wrongly, so the raw image is made with `objcopy`.
  - **Privacy** (the owner's addendum, `docs/prompts/M0d-addendum.md`):
    no private term (username, real name, e-mail, hostname, local folder
    names) in the repository. `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE,
    R-PUB-3) scans tracked files and commit messages against terms the
    owner keeps in the gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` and the
    `PRIVATE_TERMS` secret, reporting file and line only; the pre-commit
    and commit-msg hooks run it too. Records unchanged since the base
    commit `80864b9` are exempt by blob hash (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Privacy").
    `tools/archive-session.py` now redacts the username, the top folder
    (as `<top>`) and the terms. The pull request's branch was rewritten
    once, before merge and with the owner's approval, so the local path
    in the saved M0d prompt never reached main; `docs/EXPOSURE.md`'s
    older paths are redacted in its current text.
  - **Merged**: pull request #10 as `4760d561`. Its first record
    (`records/4760d561…/`) is FAIL on C-MERGE alone: the records workflow
    read the head's ci run while GitHub still reported it in progress,
    although its only job had finished with success (13:25:15Z; GitHub
    marked the run complete at 13:35:00Z). That record stays as it is. A
    re-run of the records workflow wrote `rerun-39787187755-2/` beside
    it: **PASS**, every check run, traceability PASS for R-BOOT-1 to
    R-BOOT-5, R-BUILD-1, R-BUILD-2 and R-PUB-3, firmware size code 252,
    data 4, bss 20 bytes. Since pull request #11, C-MERGE waits up to 30
    minutes for an unfinished ci run on the head.
  - `firmware/src/placeholder.c` removed. M0e is next.

### M0e: audit and performance
- **Similarity audit** (spec side): an isolated CI job fetches the GPL
  firmwares at pinned commits, compares our firmware against them with JPlag
  (SDK as base code, `vendor/` excluded, an unrelated permissive embedded C
  project scored as a control), and publishes scores and file names only.
- **Performance tracking** (firmware side): per-commit size and RAM, later
  emulated instructions per audio block. A 3% regression gate on
  instructions per audio block; per-milestone budgets for size and RAM,
  raised only by a pull request that says why.
- Requirements: R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-6, R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5.
- Status 2026-10-22, performance part (session M0e, firmware side, on the
  owner's Mac):
  - **Start**: `tools/clean-update.sh` passed; M0d's two transcripts
    archived (the archiver's e-mail rule fixed on the way: it broke a
    line's JSON when an address followed a tab escape); three of their
    commands, which only wrote text naming the spec-side folders, listed
    in `sessions/REVIEWED.json` with the owner's approval.
  - **Measured on every commit** (`tools/perf.py`, check C-PERF, in each
    record's report and its "Performance" section): code, data, bss, the
    raw image, static RAM (data + bss), the stack reserved and its
    high-water mark, and emulated core-0 instructions per period. Until
    M4 the period is the heartbeat: a one-second perf run of its own in
    fwtest, its instructions divided by the beats. The stack's mark is
    the lowest non-zero word of the stack captured at the end (fwtest
    starts RAM at zero), so the firmware needs no change for it.
  - **Gates**: the budgets in `config/budgets.json` for the current
    milestone, and a rise of at most 3% in instructions per period
    against the latest main record, whose own image is re-run under the
    same fwtest. A fall of more than 3% shows as IMPROVED in the record
    and in the CI run's summary. Raising a budget takes its own pull
    request (CONTRIBUTING.md). C-PERF-PROBES builds the firmware once
    deliberately slower and once deliberately bigger and checks that the
    gates fail each for its own reason, against the unmodified build
    measured in the same run. Requirements R-PERF-1 to
    R-PERF-5; design: docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md (M0e).
  - **History**: the records workflow appends one line per main commit
    to `perf-history.csv` at the root of the `records` branch, never
    rewriting it; a re-run adds no line.
  - **C-MERGE's three failures, and the fix** (pull request #17): every
    other check passed in each of these records, and each FAIL record
    stays as it is.
    1. M0a's merge (`2fd28219`) failed under the merge rule of that time
       (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge policy and its history").
    2. #10's merge (`4760d561`) failed because GitHub still reported the
       head's ci run as in progress after its job had passed. Since #11,
       the check waits for an unfinished run.
    3. #13's merge (`a2086340`) failed because GitHub's run search briefly
       found no ci run for the head, though its CI had passed about ten
       minutes before; the check took no answer as a failure at once.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),
  spec transcripts are skipped, not read, and the output says so;
- every transcript must show the SessionStart banner from
  `tools/session-banner.sh` with `status: OK`. Any `CONFIG MISMATCH` fails.
  The exemptions are listed by session ID in the check's `EXEMPT_NO_BANNER`,
  each with its reason (docs/EXPOSURE.md): the first session (M0a), M0a's
  one-prompt hook test, and the first spec session (M0b), each of which
  began before its folder had the banner hook;
- for clean-side transcripts, every file read, write, search, web fetch, web
  search and shell command is listed in the check's log by entry (the
  transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and any that touches
  forbidden material fails, named by rule ID (`F-...`, the check's
  `FORBIDDEN` table). The log never quotes a transcript: it goes into every
  test record, and the oldest archived transcripts still hold text that the
  archiver now redacts.

Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging: a shell command that only
*writes* a document naming a forbidden folder is flagged too. Such a hit can
be cleared only by an entry in `REVIEWED.json` naming that exact session and
tool call, the rule it matched and why it isn't a touch, added by pull
request so the owner's signed merge approves it. Agents avoid the problem by
writing prose with their file-writing tool, not with shell commands.

One kind of command is cleared by the check itself (since M1, at the
owner's request): a quoted heredoc fed to `python3 -` whose code provably
opens nothing but `sessions/REVIEWED.json` and files under `sessions/clean/`
(only `json` and `re` imported, no other file, process or `exec`-like call,
every `open()` path a literal under those two places). Its body is then left
out of the three spec-side folder rules only; every other rule, and the rest
of the command, is still matched as text. A `REVIEWED.json` entry this made
unnecessary is marked `superseded` rather than deleted; it clears nothing,
and the check fails if its call is ever flagged again.

## 1. Scope

Bring the chip from reset to a known, timed, interrupt-driven state, using only what docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md, the vendored SDK headers and the allowed FM-1-RE documents say:
- **Clocks:** set the system clocks the firmware will run at, as the spec allows, and verify them by black-box measurement in fwtest.
- **Interrupts:** our own vector table and handler entry/exit, with nesting and priorities only as far as M1 needs; a fault or unexpected interrupt is reported over the debug channel and halts cleanly, so tests can detect it.
- **Timer:** a periodic timer interrupt as the system tick. The heartbeat moves from polling to the tick, and the main loop idles in the low-power wait between ticks.
- **Core 1:** only if the spec makes it necessary for M1; otherwise leave it parked and say so in the design notes.

Where the spec gives requirements, meet them with your own design. Where it is silent or a fact is emulator-only, either confirm it with your own black-box test or file a spec request in docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md (by PR) and tell the owner. Never look anywhere else.

## 2. Tests

- fwtest suites with golden files: boot to the tick; tick period and jitter within a stated tolerance over at least one emulated second; the heartbeat driven by the tick; a deliberate fault and an unexpected interrupt each detected and reported; the idle wait actually used (instructions per period should fall sharply against M0; record by how much).
- Read docs/HARNESS.md's rules on waiting and capture timing before writing timing tests, and design the tests so their timing is exact.
- R-BOOT-*/R-IRQ-*/R-CLK-* requirements in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, traced in the record.

## 3. Performance and budgets

- The perf gate compares against the latest main record, so the expected drop in instructions per period shows as an improvement. Code size will grow: if it exceeds the M0 budgets, move to M1 budgets in their own small PR first (What/Why/How/Result), with headroom you justify.
- Startup now uses the stack before the fill runs (if it does): move the fill earlier or measure startup separately, and say which in the design notes.

## 4. Records and notes

- DESIGN-NOTES.md entries for each choice (clock settings, vector table layout, handler conventions, tick period, idle), citing HW IDs, SDK files or your experiments; PROVENANCE.md for every source used.
- Small commits and PRs with the What/Why/How/Result/Sources/Exposure template.

## Done when

- The firmware boots to a periodic tick with the heartbeat on it and idles between ticks; faults and stray interrupts are caught.
- All suites pass deterministically in CI; the record is PASS with traceability; the audit passes; budgets hold.
- PLAN.md records M1's results and says M2 (screen) is next.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Don't archive your own transcript.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),
  spec transcripts are skipped, not read, and the output says so;
- every transcript must show the SessionStart banner from
  `tools/session-banner.sh` with `status: OK`. Any `CONFIG MISMATCH` fails.
  The exemptions are listed by session ID in the check's `EXEMPT_NO_BANNER`,
  each with its reason (docs/EXPOSURE.md): the first session (M0a), M0a's
  one-prompt hook test, and the first spec session (M0b), each of which
  began before its folder had the banner hook;
- for clean-side transcripts, every file read, write, search, web fetch, web
  search and shell command is listed in the check's log by entry (the
  transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and any that touches
  forbidden material fails, named by rule ID (`F-...`, the check's
  `FORBIDDEN` table). The log never quotes a transcript: it goes into every
  test record, and the oldest archived transcripts still hold text that the
  archiver now redacts.

Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging: a shell command that only
*writes* a document naming a forbidden folder is flagged too. Such a hit can
be cleared only by an entry in `REVIEWED.json` naming that exact session and
tool call, the rule it matched and why it isn't a touch, added by pull
request so the owner's signed merge approves it. Agents avoid the problem by
writing prose with their file-writing tool, not with shell commands.

One kind of command is cleared by the check itself (since M1, at the
owner's request): a quoted heredoc fed to `python3 -` whose code provably
opens nothing but `sessions/REVIEWED.json` and files under `sessions/clean/`
(only `json` and `re` imported, no other file, process or `exec`-like call,
every `open()` path a literal under those two places). Its body is then left
out of the three spec-side folder rules only; every other rule, and the rest
of the command, is still matched as text. A `REVIEWED.json` entry this made
unnecessary is marked `superseded` rather than deleted; it clears nothing,
and the check fails if its call is ever flagged again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Checks archived session transcripts (R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3, R-CLEAN-5;
check C-TRANSCRIPTS).

  check-transcripts.py [SESSIONS_DIR]        (default: sessions/)

Each archived session is `<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` under
SESSIONS_DIR (role clean or spec, and the folder must match the name), with
its redaction note `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside it, and any subagent
transcripts in `<same name>.subagents/*.jsonl`.

Spec-side transcripts (`spec/`) are left out of clean folders. When `spec/`
isn't on disk, they are skipped, never looked for elsewhere, and the output
says so.

For every transcript:
  - the SessionStart banner (tools/session-banner.sh) must be there, with
    `status: OK` and exit code 0. Any CONFIG MISMATCH or failed SessionStart
    hook fails. (EXEMPT_NO_BANNER lists the only sessions allowed to have
    none, and why.)
For every clean-side transcript, including its subagents:
  - every file read, write, search, web fetch, web search and shell command
    is listed, and any that touches FORBIDDEN fails, unless that exact tool
    call is in sessions/REVIEWED.json (a reviewed false positive, such as a
    shell command that only writes a document naming a forbidden folder).
    Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging, with one narrow
    exception for the three spec-side folder rules (EXEMPT_PATHS): the body
    of a quoted heredoc fed to `python3 -` is left out of their matching
    when it is code that provably opens nothing but sessions/REVIEWED.json
    and files under sessions/clean/ (exempt_heredoc). Every other rule, and
    the rest of the command, is still matched as text.
  - A REVIEWED.json entry may be marked `superseded` (the exception above
    now clears its call). It no longer clears anything, and the check fails
    if its call is still flagged, so the mark can't be wrong.

The output never quotes a transcript: calls are listed by file, entry
(the transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and hits by rule ID
(FORBIDDEN), so nothing a session typed reaches a log or a record.

The format is Claude Code's JSONL transcript: tool calls are `tool_use`
blocks inside `type: "assistant"` entries; hook output is an `attachment`
entry with `hookEvent: "SessionStart"`, `stdout` and `exitCode` (PROVENANCE
P-6). Other entries are not inspected for tool use.
"""
import ast
import glob
import json
import os
import posixpath
import re
import sys

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-(clean|spec)-([0-9a-f-]{36})\.jsonl$")
BANNER_START = "=== small-beeps session banner v1 ==="

EXEMPT_NO_BANNER = {
    "36860ab8-77fd-4fd6-aa1d-2063c15a5548":
        "M0a, the first session: it began before tools/session-banner.sh and "
        "its hook existed (docs/EXPOSURE.md, Addendum 2 step 5)",
    "ddebd686-9190-4fa3-b217-30d0a98fda69":
        "a one-prompt `claude -p` run started by M0a in its scratch folder to "
        "learn how hook output is stored; its only hook printed a test marker, "
        "and it made no tool calls (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0a)",
    "e74c69f7-ff95-4dcc-bf7a-9a980e62a6f9":
        "M0b, the first spec-side session: it began under the owner's hand-made "
        "settings, before tools/spec-setup.sh installed the banner hook in its "
        "folder (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0b)",
}
ROLES = ("clean", "spec")

# Mirrors CONTRIBUTING.md, "Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or
# quotes". Each pattern is matched, case-insensitively, against the targets
# of reads, searches, fetches and shell commands (not against the contents
# a session writes).
FORBIDDEN = [
    ("F-FELUCCA", "Felucca and firmwares built on it", r"felucca|hortator|ghoulbox|melodee|\bskiff\b"),
    ("F-HUGELTON", "hugelton (Felucca's author)", r"hugelton"),
    ("F-DINGHY", "dinghy", r"dinghy|zvenson"),
    ("F-FM1-SID", "FM-1 SID firmware", r"fm1-sid"),
    ("F-PROBE", "emulator probe source", r"probes/lcdtest\.c"),
    ("F-EMU-REPO", "F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository", r"fm1-emu|f-emulator"),
    ("F-EMU-CRATES", "emulator crates", r"\bcrates/fm1-"),
    # A path into the folder, or the folder itself as a whole word.
    ("F-VENDOR-EMU", "vendor/emulator/ (spec side)", r"(^|[\s\"'=:/])vendor/emulator(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("F-HARNESS", "harness/ source (spec side)", r"(^|[\s\"'=:/])harness(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("F-FWHUB", "thefirmwarehub.com", r"thefirmwarehub\.com"),
    ("F-SPEC-SESSIONS", "spec-side session transcripts", r"sessions/spec(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("F-RE-FIRMWARE", "FM-1-RE firmware images or disassembly",
     r"fm-1-re.*(firmware-images|disasm|disassembl|ghidra|\.idb\b|\.i64\b|functions)"
     r"|firmware-images/"),
    ("F-STOCK", "M-VAVE stock firmware", r"m-?vave.*\.(fwsc|bin|ufw|hex)\b"),
]
FORBIDDEN_RE = [(rid, why, re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE)) for rid, why, p in FORBIDDEN]
RULE_ID = {why: rid for rid, why, _ in FORBIDDEN}
# The rules a heredoc's body can be cleared of (exempt_heredoc).
FOLDER_RULES = ("F-VENDOR-EMU", "F-HARNESS", "F-SPEC-SESSIONS")


def targets(name, inp):
    """Returns (kind, target) pairs for one tool call."""
    s = lambda k: str(inp.get(k, "")) if inp.get(k) is not None else ""
    if name == "Read":
        return [("read", s("file_path"))]
    if name in ("Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"):
        return [("write", s("file_path") or s("notebook_path"))]
    if name == "Grep":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("glob"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "Glob":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "WebFetch":
        return [("fetch", s("url"))]
    if name == "WebSearch":
        return [("web-search", s("query"))]
    if name == "Bash":
        return [("shell", s("command"))]
    if name in ("Agent", "Task"):
        return [("agent", s("description"))]
    if name.startswith("mcp__"):
        out = []
        for k, v in sorted(inp.items()):
            if isinstance(v, str) and (k in ("url", "path", "file_path", "query")
                                       or v.startswith("http")):
                out.append(("mcp", "%s=%s" % (k, v)))
        return out
    return []


# What an exempt heredoc may open: the reviewed list and archived clean
# transcripts, nothing else.
EXEMPT_PATHS = ("sessions/REVIEWED.json", "sessions/clean/")
HEREDOC_RE = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"])([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1")
PYTHON_STDIN = re.compile(r"^\s*python3?(\.\d+)?(\s+-[IEsSBu]+)*\s+-\s*$")
# Names a cleared heredoc may call; anything else (exec, eval, getattr,
# __import__, compile, ...) means no exemption. Only json and re may be
# imported, so no module that reaches files or processes is in reach.
SAFE_CALLS = {"print", "len", "any", "all", "sorted", "set", "list", "dict", "tuple",
              "str", "int", "bool", "repr", "enumerate", "range", "isinstance",
              "min", "max", "sum", "zip", "open"}

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Rebuilds a commit in its own pinned container and compares the outputs'
# SHA-256s with that commit's test record (R-REPRO-4).
#
#   tools/reproduce <commit> [--records-ref REF]
#
# The record comes from the `records` branch (fetched from origin, or a local
# branch of that name, or REF). The commit's files are exported with
# `git archive` into a temporary folder, so the build uses that commit's own
# Dockerfile and build script, and nothing from your working tree. In a
# blob-less clean clone, git may download the commit's other files to do
# this; the spec-side folders are excluded.
set -eu

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <commit> [--records-ref REF]" >&2; exit 2; }
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
commit=$1
ref=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--records-ref" ] && ref=${3:-}

full=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$commit^{commit}")
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    if git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin records 2>/dev/null; then ref=FETCH_HEAD
    else ref=records; fi
fi
if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$ref:records/$full/report.json" > "$work/report.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "no record for $full on $ref" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "commit:  $full"
echo "record:  $ref:records/$full/report.json"

mkdir "$work/src"
# Spec-side folders aren't needed to build, and must not land on a clean

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Rebuilds a commit in its own pinned container and compares the outputs'
# SHA-256s with that commit's test record (R-REPRO-4).
#
#   tools/reproduce <commit> [--records-ref REF]
#
# The record comes from the `records` branch (fetched from origin, or a local
# branch of that name, or REF). The commit's files are exported with
# `git archive` into a temporary folder, so the build uses that commit's own
# Dockerfile and build script, and nothing from your working tree. In a
# blob-less clean clone, git may download the commit's other files to do
# this; the spec-side folders are excluded.
set -eu

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <commit> [--records-ref REF]" >&2; exit 2; }
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
commit=$1
ref=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--records-ref" ] && ref=${3:-}

full=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$commit^{commit}")
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    if git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin records 2>/dev/null; then ref=FETCH_HEAD
    else ref=records; fi
fi
if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$ref:records/$full/report.json" > "$work/report.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "no record for $full on $ref" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "commit:  $full"
echo "record:  $ref:records/$full/report.json"

mkdir "$work/src"
# Spec-side folders aren't needed to build, and must not land on a clean
# machine (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Barriers").
git -C "$ROOT" archive "$full" -- . ':(exclude)vendor/emulator' ':(exclude)harness' ':(exclude)sessions/spec' \
    | tar -x -C "$work/src"
sh "$work/src/tools/build.sh" build --out "$work/out"
"$(sh "$ROOT/tools/find-python.sh")" -I "$ROOT/tools/record.py" compare --record "$work/report.json" --outputs "$work/out"

"""Loads the tools (whose file names have hyphens) as modules for tests."""
import importlib.util
import os

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

# tools/clean-setup.sh from this checkout's HEAD, and checks that
#   - vendor/emulator/, harness/ and sessions/spec/ are not on disk;
#   - none of their files' contents are in its .git (a blob-less clone that
#     never fetched them);
#   - its live settings are config/claude/clean.json, which denies reading
#     all three, and the session banner says OK;
#   - its .git/info/attributes marks all three -diff.
#   - the firmware side's own tools, run inside it with git's lazy fetching
#     off as clean sessions run (the tool tests, the transcript, term and spec
#     checks, the emulator pin check, and `git log -p` over this branch,
#     which must fail rather than fetch), fetch none of those contents;
#   - tools/clean-update.sh stops when a spec-side output reaches .git
#     through another branch (as the records branch holds them);
#   - tools/clean-update.sh brings a clean folder made at HEAD's parent up to
#     HEAD with the same results, and updates one across a commit (made here)
#     that changes vendor/emulator/ and harness/ without fetching any of
#     their blobs, while a plain merge with its summary does fetch some.
# It never reads those folders' contents itself: only their file lists and
# object IDs, from this checkout's history. In a clean folder it says SKIP
# and does nothing: it needs the full history to serve the copy it checks.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ ! -d "$ROOT/vendor/emulator" ] || [ "$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null)" = clean ]; then
    echo "SKIP: this is a clean folder (it can't serve the spec-side files a check would need)"
    exit 0
fi
EXCLUDED="vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec"
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail=0
bad() { echo "FAIL: $*"; fail=1; }

head=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)
# A bare copy that serves partial clones (a plain local clone would copy every
# object and ignore --filter).
git clone -q --bare --no-local "$ROOT" "$work/src.git"
git -C "$work/src.git" config uploadpack.allowFilter true
git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/checked "$head"

SETUP_SOURCE="file://$work/src.git" SETUP_REF=checked \
    sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" "$work/clean" > "$work/setup.log" 2>&1 || {
    cat "$work/setup.log"; bad "tools/clean-setup.sh failed"; exit 1; }
clean="$work/clean"
[ "$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$head" ] || bad "the clean folder is not at $head"

for p in $EXCLUDED; do
    if [ -e "$clean/$p" ]; then bad "$p is on disk"; else echo "absent:   $p"; fi
done

# Every blob under the excluded paths at HEAD must be missing from the clean
# folder's objects (checked without fetching: --missing=print lists them).
no_blobs() {
    missing=$(git -C "$clean" rev-list --objects --missing=print HEAD -- $EXCLUDED | sed -n 's/^?//p' | sort -u)
    for p in $EXCLUDED; do
        for oid in $(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' | sort -u); do
            if ! printf '%s\n' "$missing" | grep -qx "$oid"; then
                bad "$1: a blob under $p is in the clean folder's .git ($oid)"
            fi
        done
        n=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | grep -c . || true)
        echo "no blobs ($1): $p ($n files at HEAD)"
    done
}
no_blobs "after setup"

live="$clean/.claude/settings.json"
if cmp -s "$live" "$ROOT/config/claude/clean.json"; then echo "settings: config/claude/clean.json"
else bad "the live settings are not config/claude/clean.json"; fi
for rule in 'Read(./vendor/emulator/**)' 'Read(./harness/**)' 'Read(./sessions/spec/**)'; do
    if grep -qF "\"$rule\"" "$live"; then echo "denied:   $rule"; else bad "settings lack $rule"; fi
done
attrs="$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/info/attributes"
for p in $EXCLUDED; do
    grep -qxF "/$p/** -diff" "$attrs" || bad "$attrs lacks /$p/** -diff"
done

# The firmware side's tools, run inside the clean folder, must not fetch them.
py=$(sh "$ROOT/tools/find-python.sh")
base=$(git -C "$ROOT" merge-base HEAD "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q origin/main || echo HEAD)")
(cd "$clean" && GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 COMMIT_RANGE="$base..HEAD" "$py" tools/record.py run --out "$work/inside" \
    --only C-UNIT,C-TRANSCRIPTS,C-SEP-TERMS,C-SPEC-LINT,C-EMU-PIN,C-CLEAN-FOLDER,C-FWTEST-PIN) > "$work/inside.log" 2>&1 \
    || { cat "$work/inside.log"; bad "the firmware side's checks failed inside the clean folder"; }
grep -E '^C-' "$work/inside.log" | sed 's/^/inside:   /'
if GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$clean" log -p "$base..HEAD" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "git log -p: needed no excluded file"
else

no_blobs "after the tools and git log -p"

if parent=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse -q --verify "HEAD~1"); then
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/old "$parent"
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/main "$head"

        echo "update:   $(tail -1 "$work/update.log")"

# new contents and one file is added (made-up text; nothing is read from the
# folders but one file name each). tools/clean-update.sh must bring none of

# goes to /dev/null, since it names the files.
src="$work/src.git"
idx="$work/probe.index"
GIT_INDEX_FILE=$idx git -C "$src" read-tree "$head"

        --cacheinfo "100644,$added,$p/clean-update-probe.txt"
done

    "$(GIT_INDEX_FILE=$idx git -C "$src" write-tree)" -p "$head" -m "probe: change both folders")
git -C "$src" update-ref refs/heads/main "$probe"
# Every blob under the two folders at HEAD or at the probe commit.
probe_blobs=$( (git -C "$src" ls-tree -r "$head" -- vendor/emulator harness
                git -C "$src" ls-tree -r "$probe" -- vendor/emulator harness) | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' | sort -u)

input.new_string:
# (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Barriers"). `git archive` can't be used: in a blob-less
# clone with lazy fetching on, it downloads every file of the commit into
# .git, the spec-side folders' too, even with a pathspec that leaves them out
# (found in M2). So the file list comes from the trees (which a blob-less
# clone has), and each file is read by its own object ID: only the files
# kept are ever asked for, and a missing one is downloaded alone.
export_tree() {
    out=$2
    GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r "$1" | while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r meta path; do
        case "$path" in vendor/emulator/*|harness/*|sessions/spec/*) continue ;; esac
        set -- $meta   # mode, type, object ID
        [ "$2" = blob ] || continue
        mkdir -p "$out/$(dirname "$path")"
        if [ "$1" = 120000 ]; then
            ln -s "$(env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" cat-file blob "$3")" "$out/$path"
        else
            env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" cat-file blob "$3" > "$out/$path"
            [ "$1" != 100755 ] || chmod +x "$out/$path"
        fi
    done
}

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Rebuilds a commit in its own pinned container and compares the outputs'
# SHA-256s with that commit's test record (R-REPRO-4).
#
#   tools/reproduce <commit> [--records-ref REF]
#
# The record comes from the `records` branch (fetched from origin, or a local
# branch of that name, or REF). The commit's files are exported with
# `git archive` into a temporary folder, so the build uses that commit's own
# Dockerfile and build script, and nothing from your working tree. In a
# blob-less clean clone, git may download the commit's other files to do
# this; the spec-side folders are excluded.
set -eu

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <commit> [--records-ref REF]" >&2; exit 2; }
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)

# Exports COMMIT's files, all but the spec-side folders, into DIR. Spec-side
# folders aren't needed to build, and must not land on a clean machine
# (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Barriers"). Every path kept is named, because with an
# exclude pathspec `git archive` still reads the excluded files, and in a
# blob-less clone with lazy fetching on it downloads them into .git (found
# in M2). Reading the trees to name the paths needs no file contents.
export_tree() {
    keep=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree --name-only "$1"
           for d in vendor sessions; do GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree --name-only "$1" "$d/"; done)
    keep=$(printf '%s\n' "$keep" | grep -vxE 'vendor|sessions|vendor/emulator|harness|sessions/spec')
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # the tree's names have no spaces
    git -C "$ROOT" archive -o "$2.tar" "$1" -- $keep
    tar -x -C "$2" -f "$2.tar"
    rm -f "$2.tar"
}
if [ "$1" = "--export-only" ]; then   # for tests: tools/reproduce --export-only COMMIT DIR
    export_tree "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$2^{commit}")" "$3"
    exit 0
fi
commit=$1
ref=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--records-ref" ] && ref=${3:-}

full=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$commit^{commit}")
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    if git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin records 2>/dev/null; then ref=FETCH_HEAD
    else ref=records; fi
fi
if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$ref:records/$full/report.json" > "$work/report.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "no record for $full on $ref" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "commit:  $full"
echo "record:  $ref:records/$full/report.json"

mkdir "$work/src"
export_tree "$full" "$work/src"
sh "$work/src/tools/build.sh" build --out "$work/out"
"$(sh "$ROOT/tools/find-python.sh")" -I "$ROOT/tools/record.py" compare --record "$work/report.json" --outputs "$work/out"

"""Makes the M1 release SBOM from the M0 one as a template: same packages,
the file list rebuilt from the exported tree at the tag."""
import hashlib, json, os, sys, datetime

template, src, tag, commit, out = sys.argv[1:6]
d = json.load(open(template))
d["name"] = "small-beeps %s" % tag
d["documentNamespace"] = "https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps/releases/%s/sbom/%s" % (tag, commit)
d["creationInfo"]["created"] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
d["creationInfo"]["comment"] = ("app.bin and app.elf were built by CI from commit %s and rebuilt bit for bit locally." % commit)
pk = d["packages"][0]
pk["versionInfo"] = "%s (%s)" % (tag, commit)
pk["downloadLocation"] = "git+https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps@%s" % commit

def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()

files, rels = [], [r for r in d["relationships"] if r["relationshipType"] == "DESCRIBES"]
ours = sorted(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dp, f), src)
              for dp, _, fs in os.walk(os.path.join(src, "firmware")) for f in fs)
for i, f in enumerate(ours):
    files.append({"SPDXID": "SPDXRef-src-%d" % i, "fileName": "./" + f,
                  "checksums": [{"algorithm": "SHA256", "checksumValue": sha(os.path.join(src, f))}],
                  "licenseConcluded": "MIT", "licenseInfoInFiles": ["MIT"],
                  "copyrightText": "Copyright (c) 2026 japes98"})
    rels.append({"spdxElementId": "SPDXRef-small-beeps", "relationshipType": "CONTAINS",
                 "relatedSpdxElement": "SPDXRef-src-%d" % i})
sdk = [f for f in d["files"] if f["SPDXID"].startswith("SPDXRef-sdk-")]
for f in sdk:
    f["checksums"] = [{"algorithm": "SHA256", "checksumValue": sha(os.path.join(src, f["fileName"][2:]))}]
    files.append(f)
    rels.append({"spdxElementId": "SPDXRef-ac79-sdk", "relationshipType": "CONTAINS", "relatedSpdxElement": f["SPDXID"]})
for r in d["relationships"]:
    if r["relationshipType"] not in ("DESCRIBES", "CONTAINS"):
        rels.append(r)
d["files"], d["relationships"] = files, rels
open(out, "w").write(json.dumps(d, indent=2) + "\n")
print(len(ours), "source files,", len(sdk), "SDK files;", sorted({r["relationshipType"] for r in rels}))

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources

| Key | Source |
|-----|--------|
| SDK | JieLi AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), commit `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, Apache-2.0 (PROVENANCE P-2, P-10). `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` are vendored in `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/`; the other files cited are at the same commit and path prefix. Line numbers refer to that commit. |
| RE | AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL), commit `ec832f281ca165a7d5e0722985f3acb1465046d5`: its hardware and boot documents `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md`, `docs/io/01-boot.md`, `docs/io/03-audio-dac.md`, `docs/io/08-display.md`, `docs/io/09-storage.md` (PROVENANCE P-9). Only their hardware facts are used here. |
| DS | Sitronix ST7789V datasheet, version 1.3 (2014-03), 316 pages, from `https://www.newhavendisplay.com/appnotes/datasheets/LCDs/ST7789V.pdf`, SHA-256 `8ecf0e43…5d04ca1` (PROVENANCE P-11). Page numbers as printed. |
| PANEL | The FM-1's printed panel labels, from two sources that agree: the owner's screenshot of the F-Emulator app's panel with its default labels, `docs/sources/panel-app-default-labels.png` (secondary: the app's drawing of the panel); and M-VAVE's product photo of the FM-1, `https://www.m-vave.com/images/products/fm-1.webp` on `https://www.m-vave.com/product.html?id=fm-1`, accessed 2026-10-22, SHA-256 `e610a746…df14b95`, not copied into this repository (PROVENANCE P-12). Only the printed labels are taken from them. The owner chose these two sources. |
| HARNESS | docs/HARNESS.md, fwtest's manual. It is the spec side's own description of fwtest, so it never confirms an entry on its own. |
| E-n | A spec-side black-box experiment: a small image run in fwtest (the pinned image, `config/fwtest-image`). Its result is stated in the entry. C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS re-runs every one in CI, so a cited result that stops holding fails CI. |

---

## 1. The raw image and boot (M0d)
## 5. The LCD (M2)

### HW-27: The panel
- Fact: The display is a 240 × 240 pixel colour TFT driven by a Sitronix
  ST7789-family controller, on SPI1. This spec assumes the ST7789V's
  command set and timing (DS). Pixels are 16-bit: 5 bits red, 6 green, 5
  blue.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/08-display.md` §1 ("240×240 RGB565 TFT on SPI1",
  ST7789-style commands); DS; HARNESS ("lcd-WHEN.png").
- Standing: confirmed (RE, DS)
- Needed by: M2

### HW-28: SPI1's registers
- Fact: `JL_SPI1` is at `0x00011D00`: `CON` +0, `BAUD` +4, `BUF` +8, `ADR`
  +12, `CNT` +16.
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 548-560.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M2

### HW-29: Sending bytes to the LCD
- Fact: Writing a byte to `JL_SPI1->BUF` sends it to the panel. Writing a
  count to `JL_SPI1->CNT` sends that many bytes by DMA from the address in
  `JL_SPI1->ADR`. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 when a transfer is done; setting
  `CON` bit 13 makes a finished transfer raise interrupt source 16; writing
  `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. In fwtest a transfer finishes at once,
  the DMA may read RAM or the code window, and no other set-up of SPI1 is
  needed. On the chip SPI1 also needs its clock (`BAUD`), mode and pins
  set up (Q-6).
- Sources: RE `docs/io/08-display.md` §1 (`CON` bit 15 pending, bit 14
  clear, bit 13 interrupt enable; bytes and DMA bursts); SDK `hwi.h`
  line 56 (`IRQ_SPI1_IDX` 16); E-5: a whole screen sent by DMA from RAM,
  480 bytes a row, and squares sent byte by byte, all drawn.
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-5)
- Needed by: M2

### HW-30: Command or data
- Fact: The panel's data/command line is PC8, bit 8 of `JL_PORTC->OUT`
  (`0x00050080`): low while a command byte is sent, high for its parameters
  and for pixel data. In fwtest the line's level when each byte (or each
  DMA transfer) starts decides how it is taken, and the pin needs no
  set-up. FM-1-RE also sees bit 7 (PC7) toggled with it, probably the
  panel's chip select (Q-6).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 252, 269 (`JL_PORTC`, `OUT` at +0); RE
  `docs/io/08-display.md` §1 (bits 7 and 8 of `0x50080`, which FM-1-RE
  rates medium confidence); E-5.
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-5)
- Needed by: M2

### HW-31: The commands fwtest acts on
- Fact: fwtest's panel acts on: column address set `0x2A` and row address
  set `0x2B` (4 parameter bytes each: start and end, each high byte
  first); memory write `0x2C` (then pixels, 2 bytes each, high byte first,
  filling the window row by row and wrapping to its start); software reset
  `0x01` (the picture becomes black). `0x36` and `0x3A` take one parameter
  byte that fwtest ignores (it always takes 16-bit pixels). Display off and
  on (`0x28`, `0x29`) and inversion off and on (`0x20`, `0x21`) are
  accepted, but the captured picture shows the pixels as written either
  way. Other commands are accepted and ignored.
- Sources: DS pages 163 (`SWRESET`), 188-190 (`INVOFF`, `INVON`), 194-196
  (`DISPOFF`, `DISPON`), 198-203 (`CASET`, `RASET`, `RAMWR`), 215
  (`MADCTL`), 224 (`COLMOD`); E-5: the window commands and pixel order as
  above, the picture unchanged after inversion on and display off, black
  after a software reset.
- Standing: confirmed (DS, E-5)
- Needed by: M2

### HW-32: The panel controller's own requirements
- Fact: On the chip, the controller needs: 5 ms after a software reset
  before the next command, and 120 ms after a software reset sent in sleep
  mode before sleep out; 5 ms after sleep out (`0x11`) before the next
  command, and 120 ms before a sleep in; the pixel format set to 16 bits
  (`0x3A` with `0x55`) to write 16-bit pixels; sleep out and display on
  (`0x29`) before anything shows. fwtest needs none of these delays, and
  doesn't check them: on the chip a firmware that skips them may show
  nothing.
- Sources: DS pages 163 (`SWRESET`), 184 (`SLPOUT`), 196 (`DISPON`), 224
  (`COLMOD`).
- Standing: confirmed (DS)
- Needed by: M2

## 6. Keys, encoders, the pot and LEDs (M3)

## 2. Clocks and timers (M1)

### HW-11: The clocks
- Fact: On the chip, the board's reference crystal is 24 MHz. In fwtest
  the clock is fixed: each core executes one instruction per cycle at
  240 MHz (240 000 cycles an emulated millisecond) from the start, writes
  to the clock registers have no effect, and no clock set-up is needed. How
  to set the clocks up on the chip, and which system clock rates it
  supports, is open (Q-2).
- Sources: RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §5.2 (the reference clock detected is
  24 MHz on the FM-1); HARNESS ("Time": 240 000 cycles a millisecond, one
  instruction of core 0 a cycle); the emulator model (core 1 at the same
  rate, the clock registers).
- Standing: confirmed (RE)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-12: Timer registers
- Fact: The six timers `JL_TIMER0` to `JL_TIMER5` are at `0x00010400`,
  `0x00010500`, ..., `0x00010900` (one every `0x100`), each with `CON` at
  +0, `CNT` at +4, `PRD` at +8 and `PWM` at +12.
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 15-16, 384-409.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-13: TIMER4, the free-running time base
- Fact: In fwtest, setting `JL_TIMER4->CON` bit 0 starts `JL_TIMER4->CNT`
  counting up at 24 MHz of emulated time.

  `sp`, `usp`, `ssp`, `icfg`, `psr` and `cnum` read 0. r1 could not be
  observed (the experiment needed it first): for r1 the only source is
  HARNESS.
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

- Fact: In fwtest, core 0 starts in user mode. An interrupt taken in user
  mode continues on the supervisor stack pointer `ssp` (the user `sp` is
  kept in `usp`), and its return goes back to user mode and `usp`. An
  interrupt taken in supervisor mode stays on the current stack. So `ssp`
  must point at a valid stack before interrupts are enabled.
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); the emulator model.

- Needed by: M0d, M1

  holds `0x01C7FC40` (the address just past the block) and whose other
  bytes are 0. On the chip, the loader that starts an installed app passes
  a boot-parameter block in r0; its contents are not described here (see
  Q-11).

  `0x01C7FC40`, the other 15 words 0; RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §3 (a pointer
  in r0 at the hand-over).

  offset `0x4000`: window address `0x02000000 + n` reads chip offset
  `0x4000 + n`. At the start fwtest writes the image into the chip at
  offset `0x4000`, so the window's first bytes are the image and the bytes
  past it are the rest of the chip. With no `--flash` file the rest is

  writes to the window); E-1: the first word past the image and the word

  compatible with the chip's loader. Keep code, data and stacks in this

content.content:
<!--
